title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: vignette demonstrates spatialunitroot R package, implements spatial unit root diagnostic tests transformations Müller & Watson (2024, Econometrica). package R port SPUR Stata package Becker, Boll & Voth (2025). Spatial data often exhibit strong dependence across locations. Just time series unit roots can produce spurious regressions, spatial processes (near) unit roots can lead misleading inference. package provides tools : Diagnose spatial unit roots using (1) (0) tests Remove spatial unit roots via spatial differencing transformations Characterize spatial persistence via half-life confidence intervals

what: The Chetty et al. (2014) Commuting Zone Data
title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: use dataset Chetty, Hendren, Kline & Saez (2014), contains measures intergenerational mobility correlates across 722 US commuting zones. data used Stata package’s supplementary materials. Spatial coordinates stored s_1 (latitude) s_2 (longitude), following convention Müller & Watson’s scpc package.

title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: illustrate procedure using absolute upward mobility (), variable known highly spatially persistent.

what: I(0) Test: Is the variable spatially stationary?
title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: (0) test null hypothesis spatial unit root. low p-value indicates strong evidence spatial stationarity. p-value well 0.01, strongly reject null (0). consistent Stata results reported Becker, Boll & Voth (2025, §4.2), (0) test persistent spatial variable yields p = 0.0004.
code: set.seed(42) t_i0 <- spurtest(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,                  type = "i0", latlong = TRUE, q = 15, nrep = 10000) summary(t_i0) ##  ## Spatial I(0) Test Summary ## ======================================= ##  ## Test Statistic :  3.04364  ## P-value        :  0.0011  ## HA Parameter   :  41.56  ##  ## Critical Values: ##   1%  :   2.5225 ##   5%  :   2.1020 ##   10% :   1.9393 ##  ## Test Configuration: ##   Type        :  i0  ##   q (components) :  15  ##   MC replications:  10000

what: I(1) Test: Is there a spatial unit root?
title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: (1) test null hypothesis spatial unit root. high p-value means reject presence unit root. p-value 0.387, fail reject spatial unit root null. , matches Stata article’s finding (p = 0.574 simulated persistent variable). Together, (0) (1) tests provide strong evidence spatial unit root.
code: set.seed(42) t_i1 <- spurtest(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,                  type = "i1", latlong = TRUE, q = 15, nrep = 10000) summary(t_i1) ##  ## Spatial I(1) Test Summary ## ======================================= ##  ## Test Statistic :  5.75884  ## P-value        :  0.3874  ## HA Parameter   :  9.238  ##  ## Critical Values: ##   1%  :   9.7841 ##   5%  :   8.5872 ##   10% :   7.8594 ##  ## Test Configuration: ##   Type        :  i1  ##   q (components) :  15  ##   MC replications:  10000

title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: half-life measures distance spatial correlation drops one-half. half-life confidence interval 417.7 km — indicating high spatial persistence (upper bound unbounded, sign (near) unit root).
code: set.seed(42) hl <- spurhalflife(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,                    latlong = TRUE, q = 15, nrep = 10000) summary(hl) ##  ## Spatial Half-Life Confidence Interval Summary ## ========================================= ##  ## Confidence level :  95 % ## CI Lower bound   :  417743  ## CI Upper bound   : inf ## Max distance     :  4549672  ## Normalized units :  FALSE  ##  ## Configuration: ##   q (components)  :  15  ##   MC replications :  10000

title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostics with spatialunitroot
text: can assess spatial persistence across many variables simultaneously. table shows (1) (0) test p-values several covariates Chetty et al. (2014). Spatial persistence diagnostics Chetty et al. variables variables fail reject (1) null reject (0) null, indicating strong spatial persistence — consistent findings Becker, Boll & Voth (2025, Appendix ).
code: vars <- c("am", "fracblack", "racseg", "segpov25", "hipc", "gini",            "hsdrop", "colgrad", "manshare", "fracfor")  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {   set.seed(42)   t1 <- spurtest(as.formula(paste(v, "~ 1")), data = chetty,                  coords = ~ s_1 + s_2, type = "i1",                  latlong = TRUE, q = 15, nrep = 5000)   t0 <- spurtest(as.formula(paste(v, "~ 1")), data = chetty,                  coords = ~ s_1 + s_2, type = "i0",                  latlong = TRUE, q = 15, nrep = 5000)   hl <- spurhalflife(as.formula(paste(v, "~ 1")), data = chetty,                      coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,                      latlong = TRUE, normdist = TRUE,                      q = 15, nrep = 5000)   data.frame(     Variable = v,     I1_pvalue = round(t1$p_value, 3),     I0_pvalue = round(t0$p_value, 3),     HL_lower = round(hl$ci_lower, 3),     HL_upper = if(is.infinite(hl$ci_upper)) "∞" else round(hl$ci_upper, 3),     Verdict = if(t1$p_value > 0.05 && t0$p_value < 0.05) "I(1)" else               if(t1$p_value < 0.05 && t0$p_value > 0.05) "I(0)" else "ambiguous"   ) }))  knitr::kable(results, caption = "Spatial persistence diagnostics for Chetty et al. variables")

code: library(spatialunitroot) library(fixest)  data(chetty)  # Test for a spatial unit root (I(1) null) spurtest(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,          type = "i1", latlong = TRUE, seed = 42) #> Spatial I(1) Test Results #> --------------------------------------- #> Test Statistic :  5.759 #> P-value        :  0.388  # Test for NO spatial unit root (I(0) null) spurtest(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2,          type = "i0", latlong = TRUE, seed = 42) #> Spatial I(0) Test Results #> --------------------------------------- #> Test Statistic :  3.044 #> P-value        :  0.001  # Half-life confidence interval spurhalflife(am ~ 1, data = chetty, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2, latlong = TRUE) #> Lower bound: 463653 m #> Upper bound: inf  # Remove spatial unit roots via LBM-GLS transformation transformed <- spurtransform(~ am + fracblack, data = chetty,                              coords = ~ s_1 + s_2, prefix = "h_",                              latlong = TRUE)  # Use with fixest feols(h_am ~ h_fracblack, data = transformed)

title: Spatial Unit Root Diagnostic Tests and Transformations
text: spurtest() — Four spatial unit root tests Müller & Watson (2024): Also accepts fixest model objects directly: spurtest(feols_model, coords = ~ s_1 + s_2, type = "i1resid") spurtransform() — Four spatial differencing transformations: - "lbmgls" (default) — LBM-GLS transformation - "nn" — Nearest-neighbor differencing - "iso" — Isotropic differencing (within radius) - "cluster" — Cluster-level demeaning spurhalflife() — Confidence sets spatial half-life (distance spatial correlation drops 1/2).
